name: gifski
role: Highest-quality GIF encoder from PNG frames or y4m; palette per frame, AGPL
summary: Rust CLI and library that encodes an image sequence or y4m stream into a GIF using per-frame palettes and temporal dithering, giving visibly better quality than FFmpeg's palette filters. Input is PNG frames (gifski -o out.gif frame*.png) or an ffmpeg yuv4mpegpipe. Licensed AGPL-3.0 or later with commercial terms available from the author.
use_when: Any GIF where quality matters: over FFmpeg palettegen/paletteuse
Renderer already produced a PNG sequence and you want a GIF without a video step
Piping an FFmpeg yuv4mpegpipe straight into a GIF
avoid_when: Small file size over quality: FFmpeg with a tuned palette, or an animated WebP/MP4 instead
Embedding in a closed-source product: AGPL; get a commercial licence or use FFmpeg
Real delivery formats (MP4, VP9, ProRes): ffmpeg-ffprobe
license: AGPL-3.0-or-later; commercial licence available from the author (recheck before shipping)
notes: 2026-10-26: GitHub reports the licence as NOASSERTION; the README states AGPL 3 or later with alternative commercial licences. Resolution is downscaled by default for large input; set --width explicitly.

assessment.rationale: Latest release 1.34.0 on 2025-07-13 and repo pushed 2026-06-17, so active. Best GIF quality of the options. AGPL matters for redistribution only; running the CLI on our frames is fine.
